key_insight: Reusability Reports—an article format that documents code, data, and execution details—helps restore reproducibility and reusability in an era of rapidly produced AI research driven by large language models.
problem_solved: Researchers and practitioners struggle to reproduce and reuse AI/ML results as publication pace accelerates and code/data reporting practices vary or are incomplete.
method: Promote a standardized 'Reusability Report' that accompanies publications and documents code availability, dependencies, execution steps, licensing, and metadata.
Provide a concise checklist and reporting template to make reproducibility requirements explicit (e.g., runnable examples, environment capture, dataset provenance).
Encourage community adoption by highlighting good examples and integrating report expectations into peer review and publication workflows.
impact: Clear, standardized reusability reporting reduces wasted effort reproducing results, speeds safe adoption of models and methods, and increases trust in fast-moving AI research.
visual_elements: Flowchart showing how a Reusability Report links paper → code → runnable environment (container/requirements) → reproduced result
Compact checklist infographic with key report items: code repo, versioning, instructions, environment, license, data provenance
Before/After bar chart comparing time-to-reproduce or success rate with vs. without Reusability Reports
Icon set: code repo, shield/license, clock (speed), checklist to symbolize reproducibility, reusability, and fast science
paper_title: Recognizing reproducibility and reusability in times of fast science
